Here’s a quick reference to the **long‑weekend holidays in Canada for 2023** (i.e., federal holidays that fall on a weekday and give you a three‑day break).  
(If you’re planning for a specific province, let me know and I can add any provincial holidays that create extra long weekends.)

| Holiday | Date (2023) | Day of Week | Long‑Weekend? | Weekend Dates Covered |
|---------|-------------|-------------|---------------|-----------------------|
| **Family Day** (Alberta, British Columbia, Saskatchewan, Ontario, New Brunswick, Manitoba, Prince Edward Island) | Feb 20 | Monday | ✔ | Feb 18–20 |
| **Good Friday** (most provinces) | Apr 7 | Friday | ✔ | Apr 7–9 |
| **Victoria Day** (all provinces) | May 22 | Monday | ✔ | May 20–22 |
| **Labour Day** (all provinces) | Sep 4 | Monday | ✔ | Sep 2–4 |
| **Thanksgiving** (all provinces) | Oct 9 | Monday | ✔ | Oct 7–9 |
| **Christmas Day** (all provinces) | Dec 25 | Monday | ✔ | Dec 23–25 |
| **Boxing Day** (all provinces) | Dec 26 | Tuesday | ✔ | Dec 24–26 |

### Notes

- **New Year’s Day** (Jan 1) falls on a Sunday, so it’s already part of a weekend but not a “long” weekend in the usual sense.  
- **Canada Day** (Jul 1) falls on a Saturday, and **Remembrance Day** (Nov 11) falls on a Saturday, so those are weekend holidays but don’t add an extra day.  
- Some provinces have additional holidays that create long weekends (e.g., St. Patrick’s Day in Ontario, St. George’s Day in New Brunswick, etc.). If you need those, just let me know which province(s) you’re interested in.  

Feel free to copy this table into your holiday‑planning app!
